title: Marble Maze Tilt
prompt:
Create an interactive 3D marble maze tilt game using Three.js. The game features a tiltable maze board, a rolling marble, and a horse trophy at the goal.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 12, 8) looking down at the maze board.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8 and castShadow enabled.
- Renderer should have shadows enabled, size 800x600, antialias true, appended to document.body.

## Maze Board
- Create a flat rectangular board (12 x 0.3 x 12) using MeshStandardMaterial (color: #8B7355, wood-like). This is the tilt platform.
- The board pivots around its center. It can tilt on X-axis and Z-axis independently.
- Maximum tilt angle is 15 degrees (Math.PI/12) in any direction.
- Add raised walls (height 0.5, thickness 0.2) on the board to form a maze. At minimum, create:
  - Outer boundary walls on all 4 edges.
  - At least 6 internal walls creating a path from start to goal.
- Add 3 holes (cylinders, radius 0.4, colored black #111111) at various positions on the board that act as traps. Positions: (-2, 0.16, -2), (2, 0.16, 0), (0, 0.16, 2).
- Mark the start position with a green circle at (-4, 0.16, -4).
- Mark the goal position with a golden circle at (4, 0.16, 4).

## Horse Trophy
- Load 'horse.glb' using GLTFLoader. Place it at the goal position (4, 0.5, 4) on the board, scaled to (0.005, 0.005, 0.005). The horse is the trophy the player is trying to reach.
- The horse should rotate slowly (0.5 rad/s) around Y-axis as a visual indicator.

## Marble
- Create a sphere (radius 0.3) with MeshStandardMaterial (color: #4488FF, metalness: 0.8, roughness: 0.2).
- Start position: (-4, 0.45, -4) on the board.
- The marble has simulated physics: velocity (vx, vz), acceleration from gravity component due to tilt.
- Physics: acceleration = gravity(9.8) * sin(tiltAngle) along each axis. Apply friction coefficient 0.98 per frame. Use dt = 1/60.
- The marble must stay within the board boundaries and collide with walls (stop velocity component perpendicular to wall, apply restitution 0.3).

## Controls
- Arrow keys tilt the board: Up/Down tilt around X-axis, Left/Right tilt around Z-axis.
- Each key press changes tilt by 0.02 radians per frame while held.
- Press 'R' key to reset the game (marble back to start, board level, score reset).
- Add a DOM button with id='resetBtn' that also resets the game.

## Game Logic
- Track elapsed time in seconds since game start (timer starts when first key is pressed).
- If marble center is within 0.5 units of a hole center, the marble falls in: set gameState to 'lost', show 'You fell in a hole!' message.
- If marble center is within 0.8 units of the goal center, set gameState to 'won', show 'You Win!' message, stop timer.
- Track number of resets as 'resetCount'.
- Display HUD with: timer, game state, tilt angles (X and Z in degrees), marble position.
- HUD is a div with id='hud' positioned top-left, with spans: id='timerDisplay', id='stateDisplay', id='tiltXDisplay', id='tiltZDisplay'.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- marbleX, marbleY, marbleZ: marble world position
- marbleVX, marbleVZ: marble velocity components
- tiltX, tiltZ: current tilt angles in radians
- gameState: 'playing' | 'won' | 'lost'
- elapsedTime: seconds since first input
- resetCount: number of resets performed
- horseLoaded: boolean, true when horse.glb is loaded
- holeCount: number of trap holes (should be 3)
- wallCount: number of internal maze walls
- boardWidth: 12
- boardDepth: 12
- marbleRadius: 0.3
- maxTilt: the max tilt in radians (Math.PI/12)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Marble acceleration = g * sin(tiltAngle) per axis. Friction damping 0.98/frame. Wall collision with restitution 0.3. Max tilt ±15 degrees. Marble must not pass through walls or board boundaries. Holes trap marble if distance < 0.5. Goal reached if distance < 0.8.
